questions.question: In 2020, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Harvey J Alter, Michael Houghton and Charles M Rice for the discovery of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hepatitis C virus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 2020, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Harvey J Alter, Michael Houghton, and Charles M Rice for the discovery of the hepatitis C virus**__.

 __
 
• The methodical studies of transfusion-associated hepatitis by 2020 Medicine Laureate Harvey J. Alter demonstrated that an unknown virus was a common cause of chronic hepatitis.
 
• Michael Houghton – awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine – used an untested strategy to isolate the genome of the new virus that was named Hepatitis C virus.
 
• Medicine Laureate Charles M. Rice provided the final evidence showing that the Hepatitis C virus alone could cause hepatitis
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hepatitis, from the Greek name for liver and inflammation, is a disease characterized by poor appetite, vomiting, fatigue and jaundice – yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes**.

 
 
• Chronic hepatitis leads to liver damage, which may progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer.
 
• Viral infection is the leading cause of hepatitis, with some forms persisting without symptoms for many years before life-threatening complications develop.

questions.question: Which of the following disease is caused by fungi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Ring Worm.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**Ringworm

__
 
• It is caused by fungus that live on dead tissues like skin, hair and nail.
 
• It causes Jock Itch and Athlete’s foot.
 
• A red patch that may itch often turns into a raised ring-shaped patch of skin over time.
 
• It is highly contagious and can be transmitted by skin to skin contact or contact with pets.
 
• Creams and medicated ointments are often enough to treat it.
 
• Basic hygiene can prevent it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**Cholera:

 
• It is a life-threatening infectious disease and a public health hazard.
 
• Cholera is an acute, diarrheal illness caused by infection of the intestine with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.
 
• The infection is often mild or without symptoms, but sometimes can be severe.

Symptoms:

 
• Profuse watery diarrhoea
 
• Vomiting
 
• Leg cramps

Transmission:

 
• A person may get cholera by drinking water or eating food contaminated with the cholera bacterium.
 
• The disease can spread rapidly in areas with inadequate treatment of sewage and drinking water.

Vaccine:

 
• Currently there are three WHO pre-qualified oral cholera vaccines (OCV), Dukoral, Shanchol, and Euvichol-Plus.
 
• All three vaccines require two doses for full protection.

Tuberculosis:

 
• TB is caused by a bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis, belonging to the Mycobacteriaceae family consisting of about 200 members.
 
• In humans, TB most commonly affects the lungs (pulmonary TB), but it can also affect other organs (extra-pulmonary TB).
 
• It can spread from person to person through the air.

COVID-19:

 
• The new coronavirus – COVID-19 – was first identified in Wuhan, China in December 2019. 
 
• Coronaviruses belong to a family of viruses called Coronaviridae and the order Nidovirales.
 
• Coronaviruses get their name from their crown-like shape (corona is Latin for crown).
 
• They are found in animals and birds and are zoonotic – as they are transmitted between animals and people.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a water or hygiene related disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diabetes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hygiene**__

 __
 
• **Hygiene is a series of practices performed to preserve health**.
 
• Hygiene refers to conditions and practices that help to maintain health and prevent the spread of diseases.
 
• Personal refers to maintaining the body's cleanliness.
 
 
 
• **Diabetes**__
 __
 
• **Diabetes is a disease that occurs when your blood sugar is too high**.
 
• Blood Sugar is your main source of energy and comes from the food you eat.
 
• Insulin, a hormone made by the pancreas helps glucose from food get into your cells to be used for energy.
 
• Sometimes your body doesn't make enough.
 
• Diabetes has no cure, you can take steps to manage your diabetes and stay healthy.
 
• Over time, high blood glucose leads to problems such as heart disease, stroke, kidney disease, eye problems, dental disease, nerve damage, foot problems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Trachoma**__

 __
 
• **Trachoma is a disease of the eye caused by infection with the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis.**
 
• Blindness from trachoma is irreversible.
 
• It is a public health problem in 44 countries and is responsible for the blindness or visual impairment of about 1.9 million people.
 
 
 
• **Buruli ulcer**__
 __
 
• **Buruli ulcer is a disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium ulcerans.**
 
• It mainly affects the skin but can also affect the bone.
 
• Cases are generally seen in the tropics, primarily in West Africa and Australia.
 
• Infection often leads to ulcers on the arms or legs, which can also destroy skin or soft tissue.
 
 
 
• **Schistosomiasis**__
 
 
• Schistosomiasis is a disease caused by parasitic flatworms called schistosomes.
 
• The urinary tract or the intestines may be infected. 
 
• Symptoms include **abdominal pain, diarrhea, bloody stool, or blood in the urine**.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by Leishmania, a protozoan organism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Kala-azar.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The disease** Kala-Azar is caused by the protozoan Leishmania donovani.**
 
• **Leishmania donovani:**
 
 
• It is a parasitic protozoan belonging to the class Mastigophora or flagellata.
 
• It is a human parasite that is dimorphic (i.e. shows two forms) & digenetic in nature
 
• It causes the disease Kala-azar or Dumdum fever by sand fly (phelobotomus).
 
• The disease is spread by the bite of an infected sandfly.
 
• It can affect the Skin (Cutaneous Leishmaniasis), the mucous membrane of the mouth, throat, and nose (Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis), Liver, lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow (Visceral Leishmaniasis)
 
• **Symptoms** include Cutaneous Leishmaniasis - Skin ulcers.
 
• **Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis - **Ulcers in mouth, throat, and nose, Nosebleed, Difficulty in breathing.
 
• **Visceral Leishmaniasis -** Weakness, weight loss, loss of appetite, enlarged spleen, liver, lymph nodes, a decrease in the production of blood cells.

questions.question: Down Syndrome, which causes learning difficulties and physical health development delays and disabilities, is a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**genetic disease**__.

__
 
• **Down Syndrome is a genetic disease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Down syndrome** is a genetic condition that arises** due to the presence of an extra chromosome 21.**

 
 
• Here, chromosome 21 is repeated thrice (trisomy 21), instead of showing up twice in a normal individual.
 
• The karyotype of Down syndrome is represented as 47, XX, +21 (females) and 47, XY, +21 (males)
 
• **Some of the most common are characteristics of down syndrome:**
 
 
• Flat face, round head, and typical epicanthic fold of the eyes
 
• Short, broad hands
 
• Mental retardation Hypotonia – poor muscle tone
 
• Short stature
 
• Protruding furrowed tongue
 
• Chromosomal Aberrations
 
• Mild to moderate developmental disabilities
 
• Typical dermatoglyphic patterns (palm and fingerprint patterns)
 
 
 
 
 
• Recognizing the need to support people suffering from Down Syndrome, the WHO **on 20th December 2007, recognised March 21st as ‘World Down Syndrome Day’.**

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a viral disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Leprosy.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A chronic infectious disease, leprosy is caused by the bacteria, Mycobacterium leprae.**
 
• This condition mainly affects the skin causing pale sores, bumps and lumps on the skin.
 
• It also affects the peripheral nerves, eyes, and the mucosal linings of the respiratory system.
 
• Leprosy is a contagious disease that causes disfiguring skin sores and nerve damage in the arms, legs, and other regions of the body.
 
• It is caused by Mycobacterium leprae, a slow-growing pathogen (M. leprae).
 
• It is also known as Hansen's disease, after the man who discovered M. leprae in 1873. Leprosy is diagnosed based on the number and type of skin lesions you have.
 
• **The type of leprosy determines the symptoms and treatment options. Mycobacterium leprae is a bacterium that causes leprosy, often known as "Hansen's disease," **a chronic infectious disease that affects the skin, eyes, nose, and muscles and damages peripheral nerves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Measles:**

 
 
• It is caused by a virus named as** Rubeola virus.**
 
• It is airborne diseases that occur especially in children.
 
• **Symptoms:** Fever, Vomiting, Rashes on the skin.
 
• **Prevention:**
 
 
• Complete Rest.
 
• Drinking boiled, filtered water.
 
• Good light intake.
 
• Inoculation of gamma globulin.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Smallpox:**
 
 
• The smallpox vaccine was discovered by **Edward Jenner.**
 
• It was an infectious disease caused by one of two forms of the virus, Variola major and Variola minor.
 
• In** October 1977,** the last naturally occurring case was diagnosed, and in **1980, the World Health Organization (WHO) approved global eradication.**
 
• The Smallpox vaccine was the world's first vaccine.
 
 
 
• **Rabies:**
 
 
• It is caused by the **rabies virus.**
 
• The virus is spread through the saliva of infected animals.

questions.question: Chikungunya is an infection caused by _____ mosquito.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Aedes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chikungunya

 
 
• **Chikungunya** is a viral disease that is primarily transmitted to humans through the bite of infected mosquitoes. Here are some key points to understand about Chikungunya:
 
 
 
• **Cause:**
 
 
• Chikungunya is caused by the Chikungunya virus, which belongs to the alphavirus genus of the family Togaviridae. The primary vectors for Chikungunya are the Aedes species of mosquitoes, particularly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, which are also responsible for transmitting diseases such as dengue and Zika.
 
 
 
• **Transmission: **
 
 
• **​**The Chikungunya virus is typically transmitted from human to human through the bite of an infected female mosquito. The mosquitoes typically bite during the day, with peak hours around dawn and dusk. Unlike some other mosquito-borne diseases, Chikungunya does not have an animal reservoir and primarily circulates among humans.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms: **
 
 
• **​**After an incubation period of 2 to 12 days, people infected with Chikungunya typically develop symptoms abruptly.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Culex:**

 
• Culex mosquitoes are most commonly associated with the transmission of West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis, and St. Louis encephalitis.
 
• They typically breed in stagnant water and are often found in urban and suburban areas. Culex mosquitoes are generally most active during dusk and dawn.
 
• **Carrier**: Aedes mosquitoes (primarily Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus)

**Mansonia:**

 
• Mansonia mosquitoes are less well-known but can transmit diseases such as lymphatic filariasis.
 
• These mosquitoes breed in weedy swamps and marshes. They are unique in that their larvae and pupae attach to aquatic plants to obtain oxygen, rather than coming to the water’s surface.

**Anopheles:**

 
• Anopheles mosquitoes are best known for spreading malaria. They can also transmit other diseases such as lymphatic filariasis and some forms of encephalitis.
 
• Anopheles mosquitoes breed in clean, unpolluted water and are active primarily at night. They are distinguished by their characteristic resting posture, where their bodies are lifted at an angle to the surface.
 
• **Carrier:** Anopheles mosquitoes (primarily Anopheles gambiae, Anopheles funestus, among others)

questions.question: Which type of surveillance is specifically aimed at identifying missing cases of disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sentinel surveillance.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Missing cases of disease:-**

 
 
• It refer to cases that have not been reported to health authorities.
 
 
 
• **Surveillance:-**
 
 
• It is the ongoing systematic collection, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination of data on a health event for use in public health action to reduce morbidity and mortality and to improve health.
 
• The four types of surveillance are overt, passive, active, and sentinel.
 
• Sentinel surveillance is specifically aimed at identifying missing cases of disease.
 
• 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Overt surveillance:-**

 
 
• It is a type of surveillance in which data collection is conducted openly and with full knowledge of those being monitored.
 
 
 
• **Passive surveillance:-**
 
 
• It is a type of surveillance in which data is collected from existing sources, such as hospitals and clinics, without active reporting by healthcare providers.
 
 
 
• **Active surveillance:-**
 
 
• It is a type of surveillance in which healthcare providers are contacted regularly to report specific conditions.

questions.question: Which causative microorganism is responsible for the common cold and influenza (flu) ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Viruses.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Common cold and influenza (flu) is caused by viruses.**

 
 
• Influenza is a viral infection that attacks the respiratory system.
 
• The common cold is an upper respiratory tract infection caused by many different viruses.
 
• **Rhinoviruses **were shown to be major causative agents in mild upper respiratory illness (the common cold).
 
 
 
• Symptoms of influenza can include:
 
 
• Sudden onset of high fever.
 
• Headache, muscle aches and joint pain
 
• Cough (usually dry)
 
• Chills
 
• Sore throat
 
• Nasal congestion and runny nose
 
• Fatigue
 
• Stomach symptoms such as nausea, vomiting or diarrhea may occur but are more common in children than adults.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cholera, Leprosy, Tuberculosis, Plague, Syphilis and Anthrax** are the few diseases caused by** bacteria.**
 
• **Aspergillosis, Blastomycosis, Candidiasis **are the few infections caused by** Fungi.**
 
• **Malaria, Leishmaniasis, Toxoplasmosis **are the few diseases caused by **Protozoa.**

questions.question: ______ diseases last for only shorter periods of time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acute**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acute diseases**

 
 
• Some diseases last for only very **short periods of time,** and these are called **acute diseases.**
 
• These diseases occur suddenly and last for a shorter time period.
 
• Acute disease causes **sudden damage to the body.**
 
• **Examples** of some Acute diseases are **Typhoid, bone fracture, heart attack, cholera, common cold, jaundice, malaria, etc.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Diseases are mainly two types **based on the duration** of time which are **Acute and chronic diseases.**
 
• **Chronic diseases**
 
 
• The diseases that occur over a period of time and last a **longer duration of time**, or even for a lifetime are called **chronic diseases**.
 
• These diseases progress gradually and usually end up causing long-term damage to organs and internal systems. sometimes chronic diseases become fatal and cause **loss of life.**
 
• Examples of Chronic diseases are **Diabetes, cancer, tuberculosis, arthritis, etc.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genetic or hereditary diseases**

 
 
• A hereditary disease is often described as something that **“runs in the family.”**
 
• It is passed down from one or both **parents to a child,** who may then pass it to his or her children.
 
• Examples of hereditary disorders are: **Thalassemia, Haemophilia, Sickle-cell anaemia**

questions.question: Identify the disease caused by a monkey bite.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Rabies.__**

__**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rabies** is a **preventable viral disease** most often transmitted through the **bite of a rabid animal**. 
 
• The **Rabies virus** infects the central nervous system of mammals, ultimately causing disease in the brain and death
 
• **Risks from monkey bites** include serious wound infections, **herpes B virus and rabies**. if a person is bitten the wound should be thoroughly cleaned with soap and water.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malaria** is a serious and sometimes fatal disease caused by a parasite that commonly infects a certain type of mosquito which feeds on humans

 
 
• ​People who get malaria are typically very sick with high fevers, shaking chills, and flu-like illness.
 
• Four kinds of malaria parasites infect humans: *Plasmodium falciparum*, *P. vivax*, *P. malariae*, *P. ovale*.
 
 
 
• **Typhoid** fever is a bacterial infection that can spread throughout the body, affecting many organs. 
 
 
• ​Without prompt treatment, it can cause serious complications and can be fatal.
 
• It is caused by a bacterium called *Salmonella typhi*, which is related to the bacteria that cause salmonella food poisoning.
 
 
 
• **Influenza** is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses that infect the nose, throat, and sometimes the lungs.
 
 
• ​ It can cause mild to severe illness, and at times can lead to death. The best way to prevent flu is by getting a flu vaccine each year.

questions.question: How is tuberculosis spread in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct option is__** Droplet Infection.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tuberculosis (TB)** is an infectious disease usually caused by the** Bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis**.
 
• **Robert Koch** received **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1905** for the discover of the bacteria causing TB.
 
• The only available vaccine as of 2021 is** Bacillus Calmette-Guérin** commonly known as BCG.
 
• Intradermal** MVA85A** vaccine in addition to BCG injection is not effective in preventing tuberculosis.
 
• **The World Health Organization (WHO)** declared TB a **"global health emergency"** in **1993**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• TB is an airborne disease (diseases that spread through air). Another example of such disease is Covid-19.
 
• In 2020, an estimated 10 million people developed active TB, resulting in 1.5 million deaths, making TB the** second leading cause of death** from an infectious disease after COVID-19.
 
• More than 50% of cases being diagnosed in seven countries:
 
 
• **India (27%)**
 
• **China (9%)**
 
• **Indonesia (8%)**
 
• **Philippines (6%)**
 
• **Pakistan (6%)**
 
• **Nigeria (4%)**
 
• **Bangladesh (4%) **
 
 
 
• **Dr. Harshvardhan, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare **launched the new **TB Harega Desh Jeetega Campaign**.

questions.question: Which of the following disease is not caused by a mosquito bite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Hepatitis is a viral infection that affects the liver and can cause inflammation and damage to the liver.**
 
• There are different types of hepatitis viruses, such as hepatitis **A, B, C, D, and E,** and each is transmitted in different ways.
 
• **Hepatitis A and E** are usually transmitted through contaminated food or water, and they do not cause chronic liver disease.
 
• Hepatitis** B, C, and D** are transmitted through infected **blood or body fluids, and they can cause chronic liver disease and lead to liver failure or liver cancer.**
 
• **Mosquitoes, **on the other hand, are known to transmit various diseases such as malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and yellow fever, but they do not transmit hepatitis viruses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Elephantiasis** is a parasitic infection that is transmitted by mosquitoes and causes chronic swelling and enlargement of body parts due to damage to the lymphatic system.

 
 
• It can be prevented through measures such as mosquito control and proper treatment of infected individuals.
 
 
 
• **Dengue** is a viral infection that is transmitted to humans by infected mosquitoes, primarily the Aedes aegypti mosquito.
 
 
• It is a common mosquito-borne disease that is prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Malaria** is a serious and sometimes fatal disease caused by a parasite called Plasmodium, which is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

 
 
• 
 
Malaria is most prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, including many countries in Africa, Asia, and the Americas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a rare group of genetic disorders caused by mutations of certain genes affecting the colour (pigmentation) of the skin, hair and eyes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Albinism**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Albinism** is a rare group of genetic disorders caused by mutations of certain genes affecting the color (pigmentation) of the skin, hair, and eyes.
 
• People with albinism are at risk of skin and vision problems due to the lack of melanin, the pigment responsible for coloration.
 
• Albinism can occur in all racial and ethnic groups.
 
• There is no cure for albinism, but individuals can manage symptoms with proper skin care and eye protection.
 
• Genetic counseling is recommended for families affected by albinism to understand the inheritance patterns and risks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oculocutaneous albinism (OCA)** is the most common form, affecting the skin, hair, and eyes.
 
• **Ocular albinism** primarily affects the eyes, with minimal or no impact on skin and hair color.
 
• Individuals with albinism should avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen to protect their skin.
 
• Regular eye check-ups and visual aids can help manage vision issues associated with albinism.
 
• Public awareness and education are crucial to reduce the stigma and discrimination faced by individuals with albinism.

questions.question: Trachoma is a preventable disease that results from poor hygiene and sanitation. Which of the following body parts does it affect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Eye.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Trachoma is a preventable disease that results from poor hygiene and sanitation.
 
• Trachoma is a disease of the **eye**__ caused by the Chlamydia trachomatis bacteria.
 
• Trachoma causes **irreversible blindness.**
 
• It is a public health issue in 44 nations, causing around 1.9 million individuals to become blind or visually impaired.
 
• 137 million people live in trachoma-endemic areas and are in danger of trachoma blindness, according to data from March 2020.
 
• The infection is spread through infected people's eye and nose discharges, which can be transmitted directly or indirectly.
 
• Trachoma causes about** 1.4% of all blindness worldwide.**
 
• Through an innovative, multi-faceted public health strategy known as **S.A.F.E**, the World Health Organization has set a goal of eliminating trachoma by 2020.
 
• Cataract also affects the human eyes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Carditis is a disease that affects the human **Heart.**
 
• Gastritis is a disease that affects the **Stomach.**
 
• Otitis is a disease that affects the **Ear.**
